title: Derivations extend along a formally smooth map into a complete ring
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal such that $S$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$). Then there is a derivation $D':S\to S$ with $D'(\varphi(r))=\varphi(D(r))$ for all $r\in R$. (Stacks states this for a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_B$; its proof, via the ring map $R\to S[\epsilon]=S[x]/(x^2)$, $r\mapsto\varphi(r)+\epsilon\varphi(D(r))$, lifted through $S[\epsilon]\to S$ by Lemma 07NJ, uses only the hypotheses stated here: $S[\epsilon]$ is $\mathfrak nS[\epsilon]$-adically complete and $\epsilon S$ is a closed ideal of square zero.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003) and its proof, with Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, line 9257); stated here with the hypotheses the proof uses (no locality or Noetherian hypothesis), as needed for its application in the proof of Proposition 07PM to A' -> B (x)_A A'

proof.text: *The dual numbers.* Let $S[\epsilon]=S[x]/(x^2)$, the quotient of the polynomial ring $S[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] by the ideal $(x^2)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $\epsilon$ the class of $x$. Since $x^2$ is monic, division with remainder writes every polynomial uniquely as $P=x^2Q+a+bx$ with $a,b\in S$; hence every element of $S[\epsilon]$ is uniquely $a+\epsilon b$ ($a,b\in S$), addition is componentwise and $(a+\epsilon b)(c+\epsilon d)=ac+\epsilon(ad+bc)$ (as $\epsilon^2=0$). $S[\epsilon]$ is an $S$-algebra via $s\mapsto s+\epsilon0$. Let $J=\epsilon S=\{\epsilon b:b\in S\}$; it is an ideal ($(a+\epsilon c)\epsilon b=\epsilon ab$) with $J^2=0$ ($\epsilon b\cdot\epsilon b'=0$), and $q:S[\epsilon]\to S$, $a+\epsilon b\mapsto a$, is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel $J$, which identifies $S[\epsilon]/J$ with $S$; $q$ restricted to $S\subseteq S[\epsilon]$ is the identity.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003), proof

proof.text: *The ring map $\psi$.* Define $\psi:R\to S[\epsilon]$, $\psi(r)=\varphi(r)+\epsilon\varphi(D(r))$. It is additive since $\varphi$ and $D$ are. $D(1)=D(1\cdot1)=1\cdot D(1)+1\cdot D(1)=2D(1)$, so $D(1)=0$ and $\psi(1)=1$. For $a,b\in R$: $\psi(a)\psi(b)=\varphi(a)\varphi(b)+\epsilon(\varphi(a)\varphi(D(b))+\varphi(b)\varphi(D(a)))=\varphi(ab)+\epsilon\varphi(aD(b)+bD(a))=\varphi(ab)+\epsilon\varphi(D(ab))=\psi(ab)$. So $\psi$ is a ring homomorphism, making $S[\epsilon]$ an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $q\circ\psi=\varphi$: the induced $R$-algebra structure on $S[\epsilon]/J=S$ is $\varphi$, so $\mathrm{id}_S:S\to S[\epsilon]/J$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. (Stacks writes $a\mapsto a+\epsilon D(a)$, suppressing $\varphi$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003), proof

proof.text: *$S[\epsilon]$ is $\mathfrak nS[\epsilon]$-adically complete.* Let $I=\mathfrak nS[\epsilon]$, the ideal generated by $\mathfrak n\subseteq S\subseteq S[\epsilon]$. For $m\ge1$, $I^m=\mathfrak n^mS[\epsilon]$ (both are generated by the products of $m$ elements of $\mathfrak n$), and $\mathfrak n^mS[\epsilon]=\{a+\epsilon b:a,b\in\mathfrak n^m\}$: the right side is an ideal ($(c+\epsilon d)(a+\epsilon b)=ca+\epsilon(cb+da)$ with $ca,cb+da\in\mathfrak n^m$) containing $\mathfrak n^m$, and it is contained in $\mathfrak n^mS[\epsilon]$ since $a+\epsilon b=a\cdot1+b\cdot\epsilon$. Hence $a+\epsilon b\mapsto(a\bmod\mathfrak n^m,b\bmod\mathfrak n^m)$ is an additive bijection $S[\epsilon]/I^m\to S/\mathfrak n^m\times S/\mathfrak n^m$ compatible with the projections $m+1\to m$, so $\varprojlim_mS[\epsilon]/I^m\cong\varprojlim_mS/\mathfrak n^m\times\varprojlim_mS/\mathfrak n^m$ additively, and under this the canonical map $S[\epsilon]\to\varprojlim_mS[\epsilon]/I^m$ is $a+\epsilon b\mapsto(c(a),c(b))$ with $c:S\to\varprojlim_mS/\mathfrak n^m$ the canonical map. As $c$ is bijective ($S$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]), so is the canonical map of $S[\epsilon]$: $S[\epsilon]$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003), proof

proof.text: *The hypotheses on $J$ and on $\mathrm{id}_S$.* (i) $J^2=0\subseteq I$, so $J^t\subseteq I$ with $t=2$. (ii) $J$ is closed: by step 3, $J+I^m=\{a+\epsilon b:a\in\mathfrak n^m,b\in S\}$, so $\bigcap_{m\ge1}(J+I^m)=\{a+\epsilon b:a\in\bigcap_m\mathfrak n^m\}$; an $a\in\bigcap_m\mathfrak n^m$ has $c(a)=0=c(0)$, so $a=0$ by injectivity of $c$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; thus $\bigcap_m(J+I^m)=J$. (iii) With $S[\epsilon]/J=S$ via $q$, $q(I)=\mathfrak n$ (step 3 with $m=1$), and the $R$-algebra map $g=\mathrm{id}_S$ of step 2 satisfies $g(\mathfrak n^1)=\mathfrak n=q(I)$, i.e. $r=1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003), proof

proof.text: *The lift.* $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] (Stacks Lemma 07NJ) to $\varphi$, $\mathfrak n$, the $R$-algebra $A=S[\epsilon]$ (via $\psi$, step 2), the ideal $I=\mathfrak nS[\epsilon]$ for which $A$ is $I$-adically complete (step 3), the ideal $J=\epsilon S$ with $J^2\subseteq I$ and $J=\bigcap_m(J+I^m)$ (step 4), and $g=\mathrm{id}_S:S\to A/J=S$ with $g(\mathfrak n)\subseteq q(I)$ (step 4): there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\sigma:S\to S[\epsilon]$ with $q\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_S$. This is the dotted arrow of the diagram in the source. (The discrete lifting property of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] alone does not apply here: $S[\epsilon]/J=S$ is not discrete, $\mathrm{id}_S$ kills no power of $\mathfrak n$ unless $\mathfrak n$ is nilpotent; that is why 07NJ is needed.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PL (lemma-lift-derivation-through-fs, line 12003), proof

proof.text: *$\sigma$ gives the derivation.* Since $q(\sigma(s))=s$, step 1 writes $\sigma(s)=s+\epsilon D'(s)$ for a unique $D'(s)\in S$; this defines a map $D':S\to S$. Comparing $\epsilon$-components: $\sigma(s+s')=\sigma(s)+\sigma(s')$ gives $D'(s+s')=D'(s)+D'(s')$; $\sigma(ss')=\sigma(s)\sigma(s')=ss'+\epsilon(sD'(s')+s'D'(s))$ gives $D'(ss')=sD'(s')+s'D'(s)$. So $D'$ is a derivation. As $\sigma$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, $\sigma\circ\varphi=\psi$, i.e. $\varphi(r)+\epsilon D'(\varphi(r))=\varphi(r)+\epsilon\varphi(D(r))$ for $r\in R$, so $D'(\varphi(r))=\varphi(D(r))$. ('Write $\varphi(b)=b+\epsilon D'(b)$. Then $D'$ is the desired extension.')

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks 07PL (more-algebra.tex line 12003) in six steps: the dual numbers S[eps] and the square-zero ideal J = eps S (elementary, from the polynomial ring and quotient definitions); the ring map psi(r) = phi(r) + eps phi(D r) and q psi = phi; S[eps] is nS[eps]-adically complete since (nS[eps])^m = n^m + eps n^m and the canonical map is c x c; J is closed (intersection of n^m is 0) with J^2 = 0, and id_S maps n into q(I); the lift sigma: S -> S[eps] from Lemma 07NJ, which the DAG lacked: new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete stated with the DAG's (discrete-R) adic formal smoothness, A I-adically complete, J closed with J^t in I, g(n^r) in q(I); sigma = id + eps D' is a ring map iff D' is a derivation, and sigma phi = psi gives D' phi = phi D. Checked that only the stated hypotheses are used (no locality, no Noetherian hypothesis): 07NJ's proof uses only completeness of A, closedness of J, J^t in I, and lifts along square-zero kernels of discrete quotients. The DAG's definition of formal smoothness is the discrete-target lifting property (07NI (2)(b)), so 07NJ is needed and is not a consequence of the definition alone. Statement unchanged.
